newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 28.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail:
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
SPEAKER PUTS DOWN ADJOURNMENT MOTION

Lok Sabha (Lower House) Speaker P.A. Sangma rejected a Bhartiya Janata Party (BJP) plea to move an adjournment motion to discuss the issue of imposition of president's rule in Uttar Pradesh (UP). The BJP's plan was to corner the United Front government regarding its decision to impose president's rule in UP without allowing the party form a government, despite its being the single largest party. The Speaker did not allow the motion on grounds that the matter was pending adjudication in the Allahabad High Court.
The Times Of India
TUSSLE FOR SUPREMACY CONTINUES IN CONGRESS PARTY

The tussle for supremacy in the Congress continued despite a cordial meeting between party chief Sitarm Kesri and Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP) leader Narasimha Rao. The two leaders met at a gathering of congress Parliament members (MPs) from Orissa (where Rao is an MP) and Bihar in New Delhi. The meeting did little to improve the ties between the two. Rao has been sore over Kesri's move to remove his supporters from various party posts and a call by party MPs for his exit from the CPP post. Sources said the Kesri camp was finding it tough to muster the required two thirds majority in the CPP to remove Rao as its chief, with former chief minister of Maharashtra Sarad Pawar deciding
The Pioneer
CONGRESS DOWN, BHARATIYA JANATA PARTY UPBEAT IN UP

The Congress party suffered a severe set-back on the eve of Upper House polls as 12 of its prominent legislators stayed away from a party meeting held at Locknow, Uttar Pradesh (UP). The Bhartiya Janata Party (BJP) was upbeat on the new development, expecting the same legislators to boycott the Upper House polls thus giving it additional advantage over the rest. The polls are likely to determine Congress's ability to form a non-BJP secular alliance that could produce a government in UP. The BJP has started wooing the breakaway Congressmen to strengthen its position in the state.
The Economic Times
SHORT-SALE POSITIONS TO BE SUBMITTED DAILY

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) decided all exchanges would require each of its member brokers to submit their scrip-wise net short-sale positions at the end of each trading day. Sources said the B.D. Shah Committee, set up by SEBI to frame guidelines for short-sales, had also defined the concept of short-sales. The committee said short-sales would be defined as selling the shares without having the physical possession of the shares unless it was for squaring up of an earlier purchase in the same settlement and in the same stock exchange. This information would be required in respect of 60 actively traded scrips to be given out by SEBI, sources added.
RAMAIAH PUSHES LEON TO CAP TRADE DEFICIT

Commerce Minister B B Ramaiah met the European Union (EU)'s external trade commissioner Sir Leon Brittan to discuss the ministerial session of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) in Singapore next month. The minister urged remedial action to deal with the sharp rise in India's trade deficit with the 15-nation EU. India's trade deficit widened to ECU 1.6 billion in 1995 (nearly $2 billion) from ECU 230 million the previous year. While India's exports went up by some 8 percent to ECU 7.8 billion, imports from the EU rose by 26 percent to ECU 9.4 billion. The deficit could rise further, following the EU's decision to impose antidumping duties on Indian exports of unbleached cotton fabrics.
RIGHTS ISSUE MOBILISATIONS DECLINE TO 13.98 BLN RUPEES

Rights issue mobilisations dropped sharply in the first half of fiscal 1996/97 (April-March), with only 75 companies raising 13.98 billion rupees. The period saw 90 rights issues raising 13.08 billion rupees compared to 266 rights issues (65.08 billion rupees) in same period in 1995/95. Figures put out by Delhi-based Prime Database showed 176 companies raised 51.99 billion rupees in the second half of 1995/96. Of this, 20 billion rupees was raised by banks to meet capital adequacy norms. Prime Database sources said rights offers had been unattractive as they were made at a premium and the offer price was not comparable to market price.
AD-HOC TREASURY BILLS TO GO, RBI CHIEF SAYS

Central bank (RBI) Governor C. Rangaralan sai his bank was having talks with the government on phasing out ad-hoc treasury bills. The RBI was discussing with the government modalities to be put in place after March 1997 and expected the budget for 1997/98 (April-March) to come out with a statement on the issue. Ad-hoc treasury bills allowed the government to borrow from the RBI at will, thus compromising the apex bank's control over the monetary policy. Rangarajan agreed the government would require some support as seasonal expenditure was not matched throughout the year and called for an alternative support system.
LINCOLN NATIONAL MULLS JOINT VENTURE WITH INDIAN PARTNER

Lincoln National Corporation, the U.S.-based insurance major, is having talks with Unit Trust of India, the Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India, the the A.B. Group and a few large public sector banks to forming a joint venture. Negotiations are said to be at an advanced stage. Lincoln, which manages assets worth around $100 billion, is eager to sign a memorandum of understanding (MoUs) without any further loss of time. About 18 insurance majors have already signed MoUs with companies in India.
FOOD SECTOR LURES 25.73 BLN RUPEE FDI

India's food processing industry has attracted 25.73 billion rupees in foreign direct investment (FDI) from 1991 to May 1996. The approved FDI covers fruit pulp, concentrates, juices, puree and derivatives besides canned, frozen and dehydrated fruits and vegetables, flavours, emulsions, seafood and meat products. The commerce ministry has set a target of 6.8 billion rupees worth of fruit and vegetables for fiscal 1996/97 (April-March). In horticulture, the target for 1996/97 is 29.73 billion rupees.
CHINESE PRESIDENT'S VISIT TO BOOST INDO-CHINA TRADE TIES

Economic and business relations between India and China will be high on the agenda of the visiting Chinese delegation headed by President Jiang Zemin. The Chinese delegation is expected to hold talks with the business community to formulate a strategy for accelerating the flow of investment and bilateral trade between the two countries. Telecommunication equipment, ceramics, specialised medical equipment, textiles, dairy development, silk processing, chemicals and pharmaceuticals and industrial machinery and machine tools are some of the areas identified to have significant potential for joint ventures and collaboration between India and China.
SHARE PRICES PLUNGE STEEPLY

Share prices plunged across-the-board on renewed speculative selling pressure on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) on Wednesday. Seventeen of the top 50 scrips hit the price band at the NSE, while prices at the BSE saw new 52 week lows in some issues. The BSE Sensitive index lost 64.87 points to close at 2883.57. The NSE-50 Index was down by 26.40 points and closed at 829.08. The market was dominated by speculators. ----
The Observer
ONGC VIDESH MAY BE GIVEN MORE FOR OVERSEAS VENTURE

The petroleum and natural gas ministry favours delegation of more powers to Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) Videsh Ltd to enable the company to undertake its overseas oil and natural gas exploration venture without seeking mandatory approvals from the government. The ministry has recommended the case for the Planning Commission's consideration for incorporation in the Ninth Plan. ONGC Videsh Ltd had asked the government to allow its proposals to be cleared at the Empowered Committee level without being subjected to Cabinet Committee for Economic Affairs approvals to avoid delay.
Business Standard
BANKS DIRECTED TO INCREASE LENDING TO INDUSTRIAL SECTOR

The central bank (RBI) has issued a circular to banks asking them to increase lending to the industrial sector. The RBI move comes on the eve of the finance minister's annual meeting with bank chiefs, at which the minister may call for increasing the flow of credit and lowering interest rates. The RBI has made it easier for the banks to enhance lending by allowing them to enhance the discretionary powers of their officials to sanction loans.
